chunks.text: SHRIRAM CREDIT — LAMF Application Process (Digital Validation) Customer question: What is the LAMF loan application process? Simple answer: The LAMF loan process validates and fetches your details digitally online. You complete the journey on the official Shriram Credit platform — no branch visit is required for these verification steps. Customer question: How is my information validated during the LAMF journey? Simple answer: Key details are validated or fetched digitally, with your consent, at each stage of the online journey. Digital validations and fetches include: - PAN validation — your PAN is verified digitally (via NSDL / Digio). - DigiLocker / eKYC — identity and address documents are fetched securely from DigiLocker with your permission, using Aadhaar OTP on the official page only. - Email verification — a one-time OTP is sent to your registered email for official updates and documents. - Bank account validation — your bank account number and account-holder name are verified digitally (penny drop / name match) before the journey continues. - Credit bureau check — your credit score is fetched after successful PAN validation. - MF portfolio fetch — eligible mutual fund

fied digitally (penny drop / name match) before the journey continues. - Credit bureau check — your credit score is fetched after successful PAN validation. - MF portfolio fetch — eligible mutual fund holdings are fetched via MF Central after you enter the OTP sent to your registered mobile. - Liveness check and face match — digital identity verification where required in the journey. - e-Sign and e-Mandate — loan agreement signing and repayment mandate are completed digitally via Digio. Customer question: Do I need to visit a branch for PAN, KYC, or bank verification? Simple answer: No. PAN validation, DigiLocker-based eKYC, and bank account verification are completed digitally within the online LAMF journey. Security reminder: Enter OTPs only on official Shriram Credit, DigiLocker, or Digio pages. Never share your OTP, PIN, password, or CVV with anyone — including callers.
